title: Wasted Prefill Analysis (notebook export) — eviction/pressure correlation
body:
Notebook export (copy/paste from scratchpad). This is exploratory and includes rough queries + interpretation notes.

============================================================
0) Why we’re looking at “wasted prefill”
============================================================
Goal: quantify prefill compute that doesn’t translate into cheaper/faster decode due to cache misses/evictions.

In practice we keep seeing:
- hit-rate looks “fine-ish” overall but cost spikes on specific routes/models
- operators say “cache is thrashing” but we don’t have a single metric that makes it obvious

Hypothesis: wasted prefill ratio is a better early indicator of cache pressure/evictions than hit-rate alone.

Working definition (aligned with current instrumentation direction):
- Prefill tokens = tokens processed in prefill stage for request
- Reused tokens = tokens served from prefix/KV cache (i.e., tokens not recomputed)
- Wasted prefill tokens = prefill tokens that did NOT contribute to subsequent reuse (either by same-route reuse, multi-turn, or repeated prompts), typically due to:
  - eviction before reuse (pressure)
  - TTL expiry before reuse (time gap)
  - policy disabled / route not cacheable
  - hash/canonicalization mismatch
  - version mismatch (model/prompt schema changes)

NOTE: there are multiple ways to define “wasted”; this notebook uses the current runtime-centric definition that’s easiest to instrument: prefill effort that had no reuse event within a configured attribution window.

============================================================
1) Data sources used in this analysis
============================================================
Environment: prod metrics (Hosted + a couple Dedicated tenants).

Signals referenced (names approximate — we renamed a few times; see notes below):
- redwood.cache.prefill_tokens_total{...}
- redwood.cache.reused_tokens_total{cache_type="prefix"|"kv", ...}
- redwood.cache.wasted_prefill_tokens_total{...}
- redwood.cache.evictions_total{reason=...}
- redwood.cache.memory_pressure{...}  (gauge 0..1 or bytes/limit depending on final)
- redwood.cache.hit_total / miss_total + miss_reason breakdown

Dimensions we try to slice by (with cardinality constraints):
- model (allowlisted stable model IDs)
- model_version (coarse, allowlisted; often “pinned” version for Dedicated)
- route (route_id allowlisted, not per-tenant free-form)
- deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private)
- region
- prompt_length_bucket (bucketed)

Important caveat on joinability:
- Several time ranges include partial rollout where route/model_version tags were missing on some shards.
- Streaming retries bug caused double counting in earlier builds (fixed in github:redwood/pr-18428). Any time window before that fix is noisy.

============================================================
2) Quick sanity checks (are we measuring anything real?)
============================================================
Cell: sanity check total tokens

PromQL (rough):
- total_prefill = sum(rate(redwood_cache_prefill_tokens_total[5m]))
- total_decode  = sum(rate(redwood_decode_tokens_total[5m]))  (if available)

Expectation:
- prefill should track request volume and prompt length distribution; decode tracks completion length.
- wasted_prefill should be a subset of prefill and move with cache effectiveness.

PromQL:
- wasted = sum(rate(redwood_cache_wasted_prefill_tokens_total[5m]))
- wasted_ratio = wasted / clamp_min(sum(rate(redwood_cache_prefill_tokens_total[5m])), 1)

Notes:
- On “cold start” periods (deploys / regional failover) we expect wasted_ratio to jump temporarily.
- On routes with caching disabled, wasted_ratio will look ~1.0 unless we explicitly gate metric emission by cache-enabled routes. If we don’t gate, dashboards need a filter: cache_policy="enabled".

============================================================
3) Primary plots: wasted prefill vs eviction/pressure
============================================================
Cell: correlation by time series (global)

PromQL (global):
A = sum(rate(redwood_cache_wasted_prefill_tokens_total[5m]))
B = sum(rate(redwood_cache_prefill_tokens_total[5m]))
W = A / clamp_min(B, 1)

E = sum(rate(redwood_cache_evictions_total[5m]))
P = avg(redwood_cache_memory_pressure)

Overlay W with E and P.

Observation (qualitative):
- W tends to lead E spikes by ~1–3 minutes in a few incidents.
- P (pressure) rises steadily before E. When P > ~0.85 (normalized), E spikes and W spikes.

Interpretation:
- W is sensitive to “we are doing prefill but not getting reuse”, which happens before evictions are visible at scale.
- If we alert on E alone we may miss early degradation.

Caveat:
- Need to ensure wasted_prefill attribution window isn’t itself introducing the lead/lag artifact.

------------------------------------------------------------
Cell: correlation by route/model (top offenders)

PromQL (top routes by wasted_ratio):
- wasted_ratio_by_route =
  (
    sum by (route_id, model) (rate(redwood_cache_wasted_prefill_tokens_total{cache_policy="enabled"}[15m]))
  )
  /
  (
    clamp_min(sum by (route_id, model) (rate(redwood_cache_prefill_tokens_total{cache_policy="enabled"}[15m])), 1)
  )

Then pick top 10 by current value.

For each offender route/model pair, also plot:
- eviction_rate_by_route_model = sum by(route_id, model) (rate(redwood_cache_evictions_total[15m]))
- pressure_by_route_model = avg by(route_id, model) (redwood_cache_memory_pressure)

Findings:
- A small number of chat routes dominate wasted_prefill_tokens_total.
- A couple of long-context RAG routes have high wasted_ratio but moderate absolute tokens (still important for cost per request).

Initial taxonomy (what seems to drive high wasted):
1) High concurrency + long prompts -> pressure -> evictions -> wasted spikes
2) Streaming chat with slight prompt drift (canonicalization issues) -> “hash_mismatch” miss reasons; wasted stays elevated even without obvious eviction spikes
3) Model rollout / model_version mismatch -> sudden increase in wasted + miss_reason="version_mismatch" (see Support ticket pattern)

============================================================
4) Prompt length bucket effects
============================================================
Cell: wasted ratio by prompt_length_bucket

PromQL:
W_bucket =
  sum by(prompt_length_bucket) (rate(redwood_cache_wasted_prefill_tokens_total{cache_policy="enabled"}[15m]))
  /
  clamp_min(sum by(prompt_length_bucket) (rate(redwood_cache_prefill_tokens_total{cache_policy="enabled"}[15m])), 1)

Observation:
- Buckets >= 8k tokens show disproportionately high wasted_ratio.
- Buckets 0–1k tokens: wasted ratio usually tracks hit-rate inversely (as expected).
- Buckets 2k–4k sometimes show a bimodal pattern depending on route (likely due to mixed workloads: RAG vs chat).

Interpretation:
- For long-context prompts, the cache footprint per request is larger; we hit memory limits sooner.
- Potential recommendation lever: cap max_prefix_cache_bytes per route OR change caching eligibility for very long prompts (cache only first N tokens / canonicalize retrieval section separately).

Open question:
- Should wasted_prefill be split into “wasted due to eviction/pressure” vs “wasted due to mismatch/disabled”? Otherwise it’s hard to recommend the right fix.

============================================================
5) Miss reason cross-check
============================================================
Cell: Does wasted track miss_reason breakdown?

PromQL:
misses_by_reason = sum by (miss_reason) (rate(redwood_cache_miss_total{cache_type="prefix"}[15m]))

Also:
miss_ratio_by_reason =
  sum by(miss_reason) (rate(redwood_cache_miss_total{cache_type="prefix"}[15m]))
  /
  clamp_min(sum(rate(redwood_cache_request_total{cache_type="prefix"}[15m])), 1)

Notes:
- On a few routes, wasted_ratio rises while miss_ratio_by_reason is flat.
- That suggests wasted is capturing something different than request-level misses; it’s token-weighted. That’s good (cost-weighted), but we need to be explicit in docs.

Hypothesis:
- A route can have stable request-level hit-rate but longer prompts (token mix shift) can drive wasted tokens up.

Action item for dashboards:
- Put both “request hit-rate” and “token-weighted reuse/waste” next to each other.

============================================================
6) Ad-hoc incident replay (one recent cache regression)
============================================================
Time window: 2025-03-09 17:00–20:00 UTC (approx) — known incident from SRE notes.

What we saw:
- memory_pressure climbed from ~0.6 to ~0.9 in us-east
- evictions spiked ~3x baseline
- wasted_ratio climbed from ~0.25 to ~0.55 (token-weighted)
- latency p95 drifted +8–12% in the same window

Interpretation:
- wasted_prefill appears to be a good “economics” metric and also correlates with latency regression (extra prefill compute + cache churn).

Caveat:
- Need to confirm that wasted_prefill is emitted for all requests consistently (sampling was adjusted mid-sprint). If sampling is in play:
  - counters need sampling correction (scale up) OR
  - dashboards must display “sampled” label and disclaim absolute values.

============================================================
7) Rough recommendation heuristics (NOT FINAL)
============================================================
This is for the Recommendations MVP brainstorming; treat as unsafe until validated.

Heuristic A: Eviction-driven waste
IF
- wasted_ratio_by_route_model > 0.45 for 30m
AND
- memory_pressure p95 > 0.85 OR evictions_rate > threshold
THEN recommend one of:
- increase max_prefix_cache_bytes (Dedicated/Private) OR allocate more cache memory per replica
- reduce cache eligibility for prompts > N tokens (route-level policy)
- route for locality (keep tenant/route pinned to region/cluster with warm cache)

Heuristic B: Mismatch-driven waste
IF
- wasted_ratio high
AND
- miss_reason="hash_mismatch" dominates
AND
- evictions low / pressure low
THEN recommend:
- prompt canonicalization (strip timestamps, request IDs, reorder JSON keys)
- ensure tool/function call args stable

Heuristic C: Version mismatch
IF miss_reason="version_mismatch" spikes after rollout
THEN recommend:
- keep model_version pinned during rollout window
- enable fallback policy so same prompt version routes to same model_version until caches warm

============================================================
8) Instrumentation / definitions issues discovered
============================================================
- Streaming retries: earlier builds double-counted hits/misses/waste on retry paths. Avoid analysis before fix (github:redwood/pr-18428).
- Batched prefill: hit attribution can be off when continuous batching merges prefill across requests; can distort wasted_prefill per request. Need to validate with integration test + trace spans.
- Attribution window: wasted_prefill depends on how long we wait to see a reuse event. If window too short, “legit reuse later” becomes “waste”. If too long, we under-count waste.
- Tokenization consistency: reused tokens should match tokenizer version; token mismatch can produce weird partial-hit behavior.

============================================================
9) Next steps
============================================================
1) Align final metric names + labels with observability standards + ADR.
2) Decide on a stable “wasted_prefill_ratio” definition for dashboards (token-weighted) and document it clearly.
3) Add a panel that splits wasted_prefill by dominant miss_reason category buckets:
   - eviction/pressure
   - ttl_expired
   - policy_disabled
   - hash_mismatch
   - version_mismatch
4) Validate with perf-canary + overhead benchmarks that the wasted_prefill counter emission is cheap at default sampling.
5) Backtest simple heuristics against 2–3 known incidents + 1 customer ticket (version mismatch after model update).

Appendix: metric name drift notes
- Early draft names used "kv_cache_*" and "prefix_cache_*" prefixes inconsistently.
- Current direction is "redwood.cache.*" namespace with cache_type label (prefix|kv) where applicable.

(End of export)
